clue.text: Again impeded by twisted muscle, or another muscle

indicators.note: a thing impeded by an obstacle has that obstacle stuck in its middle

parts.note: bis is the musical direction to repeat, Latin for twice

indicators.note: something twisted round is turned to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, the chest muscle

explanation.surface: A gym-goer strains the same muscle again and then hurts another one.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS holds CEP. 'Or another muscle' works because the clue has already named one muscle, the pec, in its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large flexor in the upper arm, a different body part from the chest pec.

clue.text: Good French friend collecting English porcelain

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the outer pieces take a letter inside them

parts.note: bon is French for good
E is the abbreviation for English
china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A kind French friend collects English porcelain as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china alone means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine translucent ceramic made with bone ash, a type of English pottery.

clue.text: Assume working peer to take precedence?

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A busy aristocrat expects to go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To take precedence' tells you the peer goes in front of the word for working.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on something is to rely on it happening, taking it for granted as certain.

clue.text: Chamber group: not pair playing, I start to observe

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of observe

explanation.surface: A listener notes that this chamber ensemble is not a duo.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joke is apt: a trio is indeed not a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano trio is a classical ensemble of keyboard, violin and cello, a standard small concert formation.

clue.text: All Fools' Day squabble mostly about stimulant drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier letters wrap round the next piece
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: April Fools' Day falls on 1 April, written APR I
a tiff is a petty quarrel
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, a stimulant

explanation.surface: Pranksters bicker over a pep-up drink on the first of April.
explanation.walkthrough: APRI plus TIF gives APRITIF, and the abbreviation APR wraps round E to make APERITIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic beverage taken before a meal to stimulate appetite.

clue.text: Several factors not involved with these formal concerns of nutritionists?

definitions.text: Several factors not involved with these

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
E numbers are the codes for food additives

explanation.surface: A nutritionist's list of dietary worries sounds stiff and formal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a prime has no factors other than 1 and itself, so multiple factors are not involved with these.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers divisible only by one and themselves have no further divisors, so many factors never apply to them.

clue.text: Cobblers appearing on a list

parts.note: cobblers is British slang for nonsense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shoe repairers find their names on a duty list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' suggests shoemakers, but it is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule naming who does which task in turn, a type of roster.

clue.text: Canadian city also suppressing nonsense about name

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the outer word keeps the rest within it

parts.note: too means as well

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for nonsense goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: rot is rubbish talk
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A Canadian city also hushes up rumours about a name.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers, one nested inside the other: the name sits within the nonsense, and that whole unit sits within the word for also.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the capital of Ontario and the largest metropolis in Canada.

clue.text: Knowing about a lot of historic indiscretion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: fly is British slang for shrewd or knowing

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something historic is old

explanation.surface: A worldly-wise historian knows plenty about past scandals.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly is foolish behaviour, and an indiscretion is a rash, unwise act of the same kind.

clue.text: Not partial to lose time regarding nerves

indicators.note: to lose something is to give it up, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: someone not partial takes no side
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An impartial referee is told to stop wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of NEUTRAL to leave NEURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Neural is the adjective for the nervous system, describing anything relating to nerve cells.

clue.text: Settled hill by a lake shore

parts.note: a bird that has lit has alighted or settled
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Settlers made their home on a hill overlooking a lakeside shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral is a geographical noun for the coastal region where land meets sea, a formal term for shoreline.

clue.text: Forget them playing game since things began

indicators.note: playing about with words lets the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A coach tells the team to forget their opponents and start the match.
explanation.definitionFit: From the get-go is an American idiom meaning right from the very beginning or outset.

clue.text: Embroidery accessory a bit too much on being placed in basket

indicators.note: being placed in something means going inside it, so these letters sit within the next word

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket used by anglers
OTT, over the top, means rather excessive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs rather too many sewing items into a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, over the top, is a common British abbreviation for excessive; a creel is an angler's wicker basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton reel is the spool holding sewing thread, an everyday item needed for needlework.

clue.text: Black, fetid, covering stone

indicators.note: the word for fetid is read as one piece covering another, so the top piece is lifted off to leave what lay beneath

parts.note: fetid means smelling foul
st is the abbreviation for stone, the unit of weight

explanation.surface: Something dark and foul-smelling is coating a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: STINKY is ST covering INKY; remove the stone and the black part is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky describes something as dark as writing fluid, so it is a synonym for jet coloured.

clue.text: Place to stay some eleven nights when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down-free across clue means knocked over, so the letters are read the other way
some means only part of the following words, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the end of eleven and the start of nights

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a place to stay for eleven nights after a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub offering rooms, somewhere travellers lodge overnight.

clue.text: Disorderly police raid probing unusual signs of debt

indicators.note: something probing goes into the middle of another thing, so these letters are put inside

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd
a bust is slang for a police raid
IOUs are written promises to repay

explanation.surface: Police raid a disorderly gambling den and find strange markers of unpaid debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbustious means boisterous and unruly, a lively informal synonym for out of control.

clue.text: Short-term answer having international hosted by Council venue

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone stays inside their home, so these letters go within

parts.note: the Council of Trent was the sixteenth-century Catholic council held in Trento, Italy
ans is the abbreviation for answer
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A temporary solution involving foreign delegates is housed at the council's meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Council venue' is Trent, home of the famous Counter-Reformation Council, not a town hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means lasting only briefly, passing quickly, so it fits a brief or temporary state.

clue.text: Reliable relative throttling Charlie, a rascal

indicators.note: throttling grips something round the neck, so the outer word closes around a letter

parts.note: sound means dependable
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rel is an abbreviation for relative

explanation.surface: A trusted family member strangles someone called Charlie, proving to be a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest, unprincipled person, a rogue or villain.

clue.text: American hoping Albion fails, after dropping in? That's dislike of England

indicators.note: something that fails breaks down, so the letters collapse and are rebuilt
after dropping means once something has been removed, and the word in names what goes

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American hopes England will fail, which the clue calls a dislike of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and N from HOPING, then rearrange A, HOPG and ALBION. Albion is an old poetic name for Britain or England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglophobia is the fear or hatred of the English, formed from Greek phobia added to Anglo.

clue.text: Newspaper upset secure American actress

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a rag is a scornful word for a newspaper
to land a deal is to secure it

explanation.surface: A tabloid is annoyed at signing a Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy Garland was the US film star best known as Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Male emerging from Italian lake — wow!

indicators.note: something emerging from a place leaves it, so that letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: Lake Como is in northern Italy
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man comes out of an Italian lake to cries of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is a British exclamation of surprise, used much like an astonished gasp.

clue.text: Church against restricting current Italian region

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the outer words hold a letter between them

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
I is the symbol for electric current
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: The Church opposes limits on the flow of something in an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is the hill district of Tuscany between Florence and Siena, famous for its red wine.

clue.text: Klingons primarily annoy … me?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Klingons
to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: A Star Trek captain complains that Klingons get on his nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as Captain Kirk of Star Trek, whose enemies include the Klingons, so 'me' is Kirk.
explanation.definitionFit: The speaker is Captain James T Kirk, commander of the Enterprise, whose foes include the alien warriors.

clue.text: Simple to discard one after King or Jack

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: to discard something is to throw it away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: naive means simple or unworldly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A card game puzzle: is it simple to throw out a card after the king, or the jack?
explanation.walkthrough: 'After King' puts K first. The card names suggest a single card game picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the old name for the playing card now usually called the jack.

clue.text: A good move forward, not favouring provocation

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: pro means in favour of, so not favouring tells the solver to take out that short word

parts.note: progression is advancing, moving onward

explanation.surface: A sensible step ahead that does not side with anyone avoids stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile behaviour, and provocation in the sense of an unprovoked attack is a near synonym.

clue.text: Depressing energy expressed by grunge

indicators.note: expressed here means pressed out, squeezed from the word, so the letter is removed

parts.note: grunge is dirt
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Grunge music conveys a gloomy energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grunge' suggests the 1990s rock style, but it is grime, dirt; 'expressed' means squeezed out, not spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means bleak and dispiriting, so a grim scene is a gloomy, joyless one.

clue.text: A non-professional group receiving credit for promptness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it in, so that piece goes inside

parts.note: the laity are ordinary people as opposed to the clergy or experts
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An amateur team gets praised for turning up quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity means eager readiness and speed in responding, so it matches being quick off the mark.

clue.text: Attendant at funeral is increasingly low?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a professional mourner who wails, especially in Irish tradition
second meaning: more competitive, as prices that are keen are low

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mourner at a funeral is growing more and more depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like low spirits at a funeral; it is the low of prices, where 'keen prices' means cheap ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, so a mourner can be called one; keen prices are cheap ones, and more keen means cheaper.

clue.text: I'd money for translating new Keats poem

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A translator says they were paid to render a new Keats poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Endymion is John Keats's long 1818 work about a shepherd loved by the moon goddess, opening 'A thing of beauty'.

clue.text: Whiskey concealed in a cash box for whenever one chooses

indicators.note: something concealed in another thing is hidden inside it, so that letter goes within

parts.note: a till is a cash register or drawer
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper hides a bottle of whiskey in the till to drink whenever they like.
explanation.definitionFit: At will is an idiom meaning as and when a person wishes, freely and without restriction.
